title: Conjecture (product structure with bounded tree-depth and tight clique size)
statement_text: For any hereditary graph class $\mathcal{G}$ that admits $O(n^{1-\epsilon})$ separators, every $n$-vertex graph in $\mathcal{G}$ is a subgraph of the strong product of a graph $H$ with bounded tree-width and a complete graph of size $O(n^{1-\epsilon})$.
context_text: Graphs are finite and simple; a class is hereditary if it is closed under induced subgraphs, and $G$ is contained in $H$ if $G$ is isomorphic to a subgraph of $H$. A balanced separator of an $n$-vertex graph $G$ is a set $S\subseteq V(G)$ such that every component of $G-S$ has at most $n/2$ vertices; the separation-number $\operatorname{sep}(G)$ is the minimum size of a balanced separator, and $\operatorname{sep}(\mathcal{G})\in O(n^{1-\epsilon})$ (the class admits $O(n^{1-\epsilon})$ separators) means that $n$-vertex graphs of $\mathcal{G}$ have separation-number $O(n^{1-\epsilon})$, for some fixed $\epsilon\in(0,1)$. The strong product $A\boxtimes B$ has vertex set $V(A)\times V(B)$, distinct $(v,x),(w,y)$ being adjacent if ($v=w$ and $xy\in E(B)$) or ($x=y$ and $vw\in E(A)$) or ($vw\in E(A)$ and $xy\in E(B)$); $K_m$ is the complete graph on $m$ vertices and $\operatorname{tw}$ denotes treewidth. The tree-depth $\operatorname{td}(H)$ is the minimum number of vertices on a root–leaf path of a rooted forest whose closure (ancestor–descendant pairs made adjacent) contains $H$. Examples: proper minor-closed classes ($\epsilon=1/2$) and touching graphs of $d$-dimensional balls ($\epsilon=1/d$). The authors prove that for $0<\delta<\epsilon<1$, every $n$-vertex graph of such a class is contained in $H\boxtimes K_m$ with $\operatorname{td}(H)$ bounded (in terms of $\epsilon,\delta$) and $m\in O(n^{1-\epsilon+\delta})$, and with $\delta=0$ if $\operatorname{td}(H)\in O(\log\log n)$ is allowed; using isoperimetric inequalities for grids they show that both the dependence on $\delta$ and the $O(\log\log n)$ bound are best possible, so bounded tree-depth cannot be combined with $m\in O(n^{1-\epsilon})$. Whether exponent gap $0$ and bounded treewidth of $H$ can be achieved simultaneously is open. It is known for minor-closed classes with $\epsilon=1/2$, and it holds with $\operatorname{tw}(H)\le1$ for classes of bounded maximum degree; the authors prove it for several further classes (e.g. map graphs) and leave open touching graphs of 3-dimensional spheres, $k$-crossing-degenerate and $k$-gap-planar graphs, string graphs and graphs of bounded layered treewidth. The hereditary hypothesis is essential: the analogous statement for single graphs $G$ with $\operatorname{td}(G)\in O(\sqrt{n})$ is false.

title: Open Problem 6
statement_text: For any hereditary graph class $\mathcal{G}$ with separation-number $\operatorname{sep}(\mathcal{G})\in O(n^{1-\epsilon})$, does there exist a constant $c=c(\mathcal{G})$ such that every $n$-vertex graph $G\in\mathcal{G}$ is contained in $H\boxtimes K_m$, where $\operatorname{tw}(H)\leqslant c$ and $m\in O(n^{1-\epsilon})$.
